review_method: Manual per-cell inspection of original-resolution dual oblique and fixed front/side section images; all five axes explicitly authored. No automatic labels or metric-derived ratings.

records.observation: Both oblique views show a high-walled trough/box-like gray body around a much less exposed blue surface. Large open patches at the ends are visible directly in the renders. The front and side sections place C inside the wall height rather than at an obvious usable bench top. Long lower walls remain as support, but seating use is uncertain; no definite folded sheet is resolved.

A faceted gray top spans two broad pedestal supports in both views. Blue C protrudes at a lower level alongside the bases. Front and side sections place the gray seating block above the blue plane, so the bench body is coherent while C is not its seat. No clearly detached debris or folded panel is visible.

Both oblique views show a recognizable gray bench with a thick faceted top and two broad pedestal supports. Blue C lies lower, through the support region. Both fixed sections confirm that the gray top replaces C as the seat. The main body and supports remain coherent, with no definite loose debris, damaging opening or folded panel resolved.

A recognizable gray pedestal bench with a faceted top is visible from both sides. Blue C cuts across the lower part of the support region, well below the top in both sections. The broad supports are present. A narrow pale break near one top end may be a small opening or a local edge detail; its damage status is uncertain. No definite folded panel is resolved.

Both oblique views show a recognizable thick gray bench on two broad pedestal supports. Blue C crosses below the seating top, with the distinct height shown in both fixed sections. A narrow pale opening or edge break appears near one top end; the views do not settle whether it is local damage. The supports remain substantial, and no definite folded panel is resolved.

The exposed blue C forms the seat of a regular backed bench, with gray end-panel supports beneath it. Both oblique views show a coherent seating/back arrangement. The fixed sections put gray structure around and below the blue level. No clearly separated fragment, unintended large opening or folded seat is visible.

A narrow gray slatted bench on two post-and-foot supports is visible in both oblique views. Blue C lies substantially lower and crosses the frame, with the separate height clear in both sections. The posts and feet remain present; the normal strip spacing and isolated section endpoints do not establish fragmentation or folding.

The gray upper seating strips and two post/foot supports still form a recognizable bench in both oblique views. Blue C lies below the top and projects through the lower frame. Both fixed sections retain the vertical separation. The visible strip spacing and section endpoints alone do not prove fragments, and no obvious folded surface is resolved.

Both oblique views show a recognizable narrow slatted bench on two posts with feet. Blue C lies well below the gray top and projects beyond the frame. The front and side sections confirm the different heights. The support posts and seating strips remain visible; ordinary strip gaps and section endpoints alone do not establish debris, and no definite folded panel is resolved.

Both oblique views show a narrow gray slatted bench supported by two posts and feet. C lies below the gray seat and projects out through the frame region; both fixed sections preserve that height difference. The sparse support style remains recognizable, and the strip spacing or section endpoints do not establish damaging fragmentation or folding.

The gray box base remains substantial, but blue C appears raised above an incomplete upper rim. Both oblique views expose a broad open strip and an open corner below the blue plane. Front and side sections show a gap above the remaining gray upper span. The lower support body survives, but a fully integrated seating surface is uncertain and the visible upper openings impair the body.

The remaining gray bench is visibly sparse: narrow seat strips and broken-looking thin end/leg elements leave large open regions in both oblique views. Blue C remains across a higher backrest-level plane rather than the lower seat. The fixed sections retain isolated short gray profiles. The visible interruption of the principal frame supports and large missing-looking regions impair the body; no clear folded sheet is seen.

Both oblique views show a recognizable gray slatted bench with a back and substantial connected legs/braces. Blue C lies much higher than the gray seating boards, alongside the back. The fixed sections confirm that separation. The body and supports remain coherent; ordinary slat spacing does not establish fragmentation, and no definite folded or repeated sheet is visible.

The free body is reduced to a few very narrow horizontal seat rails, a rear strip and two thin end support frames in both oblique views. Blue C remains high above the sparse lower seating rails, also clear in both sections. The end frames are present, but the seating body looks incomplete. The regular spacing versus loss of wider seat pieces is unresolved, so gap damage is uncertain; no definite folded surface is visible.

The two oblique views show a sparse gray bench frame with thin end loops and only a few narrow rails at the lower seat level. C is a broad elevated blue plane beside the rear strip rather than that lower seat; the fixed sections show this height difference. End supports are present, but the seating body looks incomplete. Whether the wide gaps reflect deliberate rail spacing or missing seat pieces remains uncertain, with no definite folding visible.

The gray roof-like bench top and end panels remain recognizable, but broad white openings visibly interrupt the curved shoulder connections at both ends. C lies well below the upper gray top in both fixed sections. The gap between top and main supports is directly visible in the oblique views, so the structure/support are impaired. No definite fold is resolved.

A regular pair of splayed gray end panels surrounds an exposed upper blue plane and a separate lower gray span. Both oblique views retain the bench-like form and substantial end supports. Front and side sections show the two surface levels. Whether C is an adopted raised seat or a suspended overlay is not resolved; no unmistakable debris or folded panel is visible.

A regular gray bench-like body with two angled end panels is visible. Blue C spans an upper exposed level, while both sections show a separate broad gray span beneath it. The views do not settle whether C is an adopted raised seat or an unintegrated upper overlay. The end supports remain substantial, with no definite loose debris or folded panel.

Both oblique views show a regular bench-like frame with two broad angled end supports. Blue C spans the upper level between the ends, while a broad gray horizontal assembly lies distinctly below it. Both sections confirm this separation, leaving uncertain whether C is an adopted raised seat or a separate overlay above a lower seat. Supports are substantial; no definite loose fragments or folded panels are resolved.

A broad bench-like frame with angled end panels is visible from both sides. Blue C forms a higher exposed plane, whereas both fixed sections show a distinct gray horizontal span underneath. Its role as an adopted raised seat versus a separate overlay is unresolved. The broad end supports remain present, with no definite loose fragment, damaging opening or folded panel visible.

The gray low-back bench and broad end supports are coherent in both oblique views. Gray seating planks cover the blue C, which appears mainly as a thin line below the seat. Both fixed sections place a gray surface just above C. This covering layer is visible, but no distinct loose debris or large unintended hole is resolved.

Both views show a regular high-back gray bench with a box-like seat and short legs. The blue C forms a narrow plane above the actual lower gray seat near the back. Front and side sections corroborate that level difference. Main supports remain present, with no clear loose fragment or folded panel.

The gray body is a coherent box-seat bench with a tall solid back and visible legs in both oblique views. Blue C appears as a narrow strip above the gray seat and alongside the back. The fixed front and side sections confirm that it is not the seating plane. Substantial supports remain, with no definite damaging gaps, loose fragments or folded sheet visible.

Both oblique views show a coherent gray bench with a tall solid back, a thick box seat and short legs. Blue C is a narrow elevated strip beside the back, above the actual gray seating plane. Both fixed sections confirm that separation. The main supports remain substantial, and no definite damaging opening, loose debris or folded panel is visible.

Both oblique views show a coherent gray high-backed bench with a thick box seat and short legs. The blue strip sits above the actual gray seat rather than replacing its top; this separation is also visible in both sections. The main supports remain present, and no definite loose debris, damaging opening or folded panel is resolved.

The blue seating span and gray back still form a recognizable bench in both oblique views. C is exposed in the expected seating position. The remaining legs/end frames are extremely thin and partly interrupted-looking; the four views do not resolve whether a complete main support frame survives or whether fine edges are loose remnants. Support and fragment status therefore remain uncertain; no clear fold is seen.

The gray slatted top and rail frame remain recognizable, with C at a lower level under the seat in both sections. End/leg elements appear very thin and partly broken-looking in both oblique views. At this scale intact main support and fine detached remnants cannot be confidently distinguished, so those axes are uncertain. No definite folded slab is visible.

The gray slatted top and long lower rails form a recognizable bench in both oblique views, with blue C well below the seating top. Both fixed sections retain the height difference. The very thin corner supports show short, uneven terminal pieces; it is unclear whether all load paths remain continuous or whether some pieces are damaged. Neither definite detached debris nor a folded sheet is resolved.

Both oblique views show a recognizable gray slatted bench and lower rails, while blue C lies well below the seat. The height difference remains in both fixed sections. The very thin corner members have uneven short ends, and these views do not establish whether all supports are continuous or whether some small parts are damaged. No definite folded panel is visible.

Both oblique views show a coherent gray slatted bench top and lower rails, while blue C remains low within the frame instead of being the seat. Both fixed sections confirm this separation. The slender corner members include short uneven ends, and their continuity is difficult to establish. Support damage or fragments remain uncertain; no clear folded surface is visible.

A gray backed bench with broad end supports is visible. The blue C is exposed but raised above the lower gray seating span and overhangs one end. Both fixed sections retain a clear vertical gap. The views do not establish whether C is sufficiently integrated as the usable seat, so adoption remains uncertain; no unmistakable fragment or folded panel is seen.

The gray slatted top and lower rails form a recognizable bench, while blue C remains below the seating plane in both sections. The narrow end/leg pieces are partly interrupted-looking in the oblique views, making intact support and fine debris uncertain. No definite severe fold is resolved; C does not appear to supply the upper seat.

The two oblique views show a coherent gray slatted bench with long lower rails and slender corner legs extending beneath them. Blue C remains below the gray seat; both fixed sections confirm the height difference. The thin corner frame members are visible as supports, and their slender style alone does not establish damage. No definite loose fragment or folded panel is resolved.

The gray slatted top and lower rails form a recognizable bench, while blue C lies well beneath the seating top. Both sections confirm their separation. In the oblique views the corner supports are extremely thin, with small uneven terminal or detached-looking marks; full support continuity and fragment status remain uncertain. The regular top strips do not show definite folding.

A recognizable gray slatted bench with lower rails appears in both oblique views, with blue C below the gray seating top. Both fixed sections retain this height difference. Some slender corner members end in short uneven pieces, so support continuity and possible small damaged fragments remain uncertain from these views. No definite folded panel is resolved.

The blue C remains the exposed seat of a gray backed bench. Both oblique views show the seating/back relationship clearly, but the slender leg and end pieces are very thin and appear locally interrupted. The sections do not settle whether those fine remnants form a complete main support frame. Support and fragment evidence are uncertain rather than assumed; no clear fold is visible.

Both oblique views show a coherent gray slab bench with broad end supports, but a small open patch/notch is visible near an upper end corner. C is mostly hidden beneath the thick gray top. Front and side sections show the covering gray slab above the blue plane. Main supports remain present; the visible corner opening and replacement layer are recorded separately.

The gray slab bench retains broad end supports and a recognizable seating body in both oblique views. A clear triangular opening occurs near one upper end of the top. Blue C remains under the gray seat, with repeated seating levels shown by both sections. Supports are present; C is covered by the gray seat, and the top opening and layered seating are visible.

A coherent gray slab bench stands on broad end panels. Blue C is visible beneath the gray seating layer, with the separate overlapping seat levels confirmed by both sections. The oblique views show a small open notch at one upper end corner. Substantial supports remain present; the gray seat replaces C, and the repeated seating layers are visible without establishing an exact intersection.

A gray slab bench on broad end panels remains coherent in the two oblique views. A small open upper corner is visible, and blue C runs beneath the gray seat. Both fixed sections retain the distinct gray and blue seating levels. The supports remain substantial; the opening and repeated layers are visible, without an exact intersection claim.

The curved blue C and gray back retain a clear bench-seat arrangement, but the main end/leg frame is reduced to sparse thin pieces in both oblique views. Only very slender dangling-looking support remnants remain beneath the seat. The fixed sections also show little supporting gray structure. C use is plausible, while the visibly incomplete supports and loose-looking remnants impair the body; no folded seat is seen.

Both oblique views show a recognizable gray slatted bench with substantial corner supports, while the blue curved C remains much lower than the top in both sections. Several white openings appear within/among the narrow top strips, but their status as ordinary spacing versus damaged strips is not resolved from these views. Fragment/gap evidence is uncertain; no definite folded panel is seen.

Both oblique views show a recognizable gray slatted bench on substantial corner posts. Blue curved C lies much lower than the gray seating top, also clear in the front and side sections. Several pale gaps occur within or between the narrow upper strips; ordinary spacing versus local strip damage is unresolved. The main supports are present and no definite folded panel is seen.

The two oblique views show a recognizable gray slatted bench on four substantial corner members. Blue curved C is located far below the upper gray strips, as confirmed by both fixed sections. White openings in the top strips could be spacing or local damage, which is unresolved. The hollow-looking faces of some corner members do not alone prove support damage, and no definite folded panel is visible.

A gray slatted bench with substantial corner supports is visible from both sides. Blue C sits below the seating top, with clear height separation in the fixed front and side sections. The upper strips contain several pale gaps; deliberate strip spacing versus local missing material remains uncertain. The corner support assemblies remain visible, with no definite folded surface resolved.

Both oblique views retain the curved blue seat and broad gray back, but a substantial supporting leg/frame assembly is absent. Small gray remnants remain at the ends and above the back. The four views support a visibly incomplete bench body with plausible C seating use but missing/damaged main supports. No distinct folding of the blue seat is visible.

A coherent gray slab bench with splayed end panels is visible in both views. The blue curved C sits beneath the gray seating slab and shows mainly along its lower edge. Front and side sections confirm the covering/replacement surface. Main supports remain substantial; no clear loose fragment is resolved, while the stacked seating layers are visible.

The exposed blue curved panel reads as the seat of a sparse bench in both oblique views. Thin end loop frames reach below its two ends, and a gray rear rail provides a back element. Both fixed sections retain C as the seating profile without a separate gray seat replacing it. The thin support style is visible but does not alone prove damage; no definite loose fragment or folded layer is resolved.

Both oblique views show a gray bench with broad splayed end panels and a flat gray seat over blue curved C. The fixed sections show the separate gray seat and curved C profiles, making the repeated seating layers visible. The substantial supports remain intact-looking; no definite detached fragment or damaging opening is established.

A coherent gray bench stands on substantial angled end supports in both oblique views. Its gray seat covers the curved blue C, with the layered seating profiles clear in the front and side sections. C is not the exposed seating surface. The open space between the end supports is ordinary frame space rather than evidence of a hole; no definite loose debris is seen.

The thick blue C is exposed at the top of a regular gray box/plinth body. Both oblique views show substantial supporting lower walls and a remaining upper rim. The fixed front and side sections place C at the upper seating region with gray support below. Fine rim discontinuities do not resolve as major debris or a folded surface.

Both oblique views show a recognizable gray bench on two substantial pedestal-like end supports. Several closely stacked gray top layers sit above the thick blue C; both fixed sections confirm the separate layered top and lower C. C is covered rather than serving as the exposed seat. The multiple top layers are visible, while no definite loose fragment or damaging opening is resolved.

The two oblique views show a gray top split into two broad panels above blue C, with an inclined support at each end. Both sections place the gray seating level above C. The thin central opening and uneven meeting edges could be panel spacing or local damage; these views do not settle that distinction. The end supports remain visible, and no definite folded panel is resolved.

The oblique views show a coherent long bench with two broad pedestal supports. Several thin gray top sheets are stacked above the blue thick C, which remains beneath the seating level in both fixed sections. These repeated layers are visibly distinct; no definite detached piece or damaging opening is established in the supports.

A broad gray bench top rests on two substantial end supports in both oblique views. The top has multiple close parallel layers, with blue C visible as a separate lower slab; front and side sections confirm that vertical arrangement. C is not the exposed top. The repeated top layers are visible, but the support cutouts do not by themselves establish damage or loose fragments.

Both oblique views show a regular supporting gray box body with the blue block exposed as its upper seat. Broad lower wall panels remain clearly visible. Front and side sections are consistent with gray support below/around C rather than an upper replacement slab. No clear separated fragment or folded panel is resolved.

The thick blue block dominates the output, with only narrow gray rails/slivers around and below it. Both oblique views show scattered tiny gray remnants beneath the span and no convincing surviving foot/leg assemblies. The fixed sections show sparse gray traces below C. With the gray body badly depleted, C use is uncertain; missing supports and visible remnants impair the object, without a clear intact folded layer.

The exposed blue thick panel dominates both oblique views, surrounded by thin gray rails and scattered small remnants beneath it. No substantial floor-reaching support assembly is visible. Both sections retain only sparse gray traces below C. C could be a seat, but its adoption by the depleted free body is uncertain; the scattered remnants are visible and no definite folded sheet is resolved.

Both oblique views show blue C with narrow gray strips along its sides and tiny isolated-looking pieces below, rather than a supported bench body. The front section has only a few short lower traces, and the side section shows disconnected lower marks. Major supports are missing or damaged. The sparse remaining body does not establish C adoption, and no clear folded panel is seen.

Blue C remains exposed, while the gray free geometry consists largely of side rails and small dangling or separated remnants in both oblique views. The fixed sections show little coherent structure beneath the panel and no credible leg assembly. Body and support are impaired; the intended role of C in the surviving free geometry remains uncertain. Visible remnants do not form a clear folded surface.
